item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 251727
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Sun Oct 25 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Vance, located a few hundred miles west-southwest of Acapulco,
Mexico, and on newly formed Tropical Depression Three-C, located
several hundred miles west-southwest of Johnston Atoll.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected over the next 7 days.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Depression Three-C are issued under
WMO header WTPA33 KNHC and under AWIPS header HFOTCPCP3.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Three-C are issued under
WMO header WTPA23 KNHC and under AWIPS header HFOTCMCP3.

$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Public Advisory Number 18
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Sun Oct 25 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 252035
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Vance Advisory Number  18
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
300 PM CST Sun Oct 25 2026
 
...TROPICAL STORM VANCE CHURNING OFF THE COAST OF SOUTHWESTERN
MEXICO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM CST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.9N 104.2W
ABOUT 315 MI...510 KM WSW OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 285 MI...455 KM S OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...70 MPH...110 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 330 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...994 MB...29.36 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests along the southwestern coast of Mexico should monitor the
progress of Vance.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM CST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Vance was 
located near latitude 14.9 North, longitude 104.2 West. Vance is 
moving toward the north-northwest near 7 mph (11 km/h). A 
northwestward to west-northwestward motion at a slower forward speed 
is expected over the next couple of days, followed by a turn toward 
the north around midweek. 
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 70 mph (110 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Gradual weakening is forecast over the next 
several days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles (240 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 994 mb (29.36 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
RAINFALL: Through Thursday, Vance is expected to produce 2 to 4 
inches of rain, with isolated higher totals of 7 inches possible, 
across Colima, Nayarit, and Sinaloa, along with western portions of 
Michoacán, Jalisco, and Durango. This rainfall may produce flooding 
and mudslides, especially in areas along steep terrain.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Vance, 
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic 
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Vance will affect portions of the coast of
southern and southwestern Mexico during the next several days. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Forecast Discussion Number 18
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Sun Oct 25 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 252035
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Vance Discussion Number  18
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
300 PM CST Sun Oct 25 2026
 
Vertical wind shear and relatively dry mid-level air are negatively 
impacting Vance's structure today. An earlier RCM-2 microwave pass 
indicated that the center was slightly elongated, with an opening 
on the southeastern side. Deep convection has been intermittent over 
the past 6 h or so, and has been concentrated primarily north and 
east of the center. However, an ASCAT-C pass indicated peak winds 
of 50-53 kt to the west and northwest of the center. Subjective and 
objective intensity estimates have continued to trend downward, 
ranging from 46-65 kt. The initial intensity is set at 60 kt for 
this advisory, based on a blend of these estimates and the available 
satellite data. 
 
Vance is moving at 330/06 kt, steered by a mid-level ridge centered 
over the south-central United States, along with a closed 
upper-level low moving across the southwestern U.S. The tropical 
storm is expected to move toward the northwest or west-northwest at 
a slower forward speed over the next couple of days as steering 
currents weaken. A turn toward the north is forecast around midweek 
as an amplified upper-level trough moves across the eastern Pacific. 
The latest NHC track forecast has been adjusted westward once again 
to reflect trends in the global and regional hurricane model 
guidance. However, the track still remains near the eastern edge of 
the guidance envelope, and additional westward adjustments may be 
needed in subsequent forecast cycles.

Westerly to southwesterly wind shear and relatively dry mid-level 
air are expected to support gradual weakening over the next several 
days. By midweek, the upper-level trough is forecast to produce a 
significant increase in wind shear, leading to further weakening. By 
late this week, simulated satellite imagery from the ECMWF and GFS 
suggests that Vance may struggle to sustain organized deep 
convection. The forecast calls for Vance to become post-tropical by 
96 h and degenerate into a remnant low by 120 h.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Although the threat of impacts to Mexico is trending downward as 
the forecast track continues to shift westward and away from the 
coast, uncertainty remains in both the track and intensity 
forecasts. Interests in southwestern Mexico should continue to 
monitor the progress of Vance.
 
2. Periods of heavy rainfall associated with Vance will impact 
portions of western Mexico during much of this week. This rainfall 
may produce flooding and mudslides across Colima, Nayarit, and 
Sinaloa, along with western portions of Michoacán, Jalisco, and 
Durango, especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
